messages:
oncall-bot: PAGER — GPU pool g1 reports capacity_exhausted + autoscaler failures. queue_length=~1200, evictions rising. paging @oncall. severity: P2.

mike: ack. joining bridge. seeing 429s from autoscaler API and pods pending in k8s for 5m.

sarah: on it, checking autoscaler controller logs. last successful scale at 3132467000, then errors: rate limit and failed create due to quota.

raj: quick snapshot: queue backlog by model type: conv-2.7B ~600, conv-4B ~400, embeders ~200.  latency SLOs breaching 95p for requests hitting g1. customers on dedicated caps getting errors.

naomi: can we shift routing to g2 region temporarily? do we have spare capacity there? :thinking_face: 

mike: g2 is at 80% but we can try spillover for non-dedicated traffic. setting route policy to prefer g2 for new requests, leave pinned customers alone.

jen: logs from node gpu-node-17 show repeated CUDA Xid 43 and oom_kill messages around 3132467600. suspect driver memory leak.

patrick: dumping dmesg from gpu-node-17:

```

[3132467599.123] NVRM: GPU at 0000:3b:00.0 has fallen off the bus. Xid=43
[3132467600.456] kernel: Out-of-memory: Killed process 14233 (runtime) total-vm:134217728kB
[3132467601.001] kubelet: eviction manager: eviction signal memory.available
```

jen: ^ that's consistent with a driver-side memory growth. multiple nodes show similar Xid 43 waves.

mike: autoscaler failing to create nodes because cloud quota for GPU instances in region us-east-1 is at limit (applied by infra quotas). we hit max_nodes=120.

raj: so two failure modes stacked: (1) effective capacity reduced by driver OOM/Xid node flaps, (2) autoscaler can't top up due to quota and rate-limit errors -> queue grows.

naomi: mitigation plan proposals: 1) cordon & drain most-affected nodes to stop flapping, 2) restart nvidia driver on them, 3) temporarily reroute non-SLA traffic to g2, 4) request emergency quota bump with cloud ops, 5) enable model-level throttles to shed load.

sarah: I'm executing 1+2 now on gpu-node-17/19/20. using drain command with force for stuck pods.

mike: issuing the emergency cloud quota request now (ticket INF-8912). added priority tag and linked incident. ETA from cloud team unknown.

jen: after driver restart on node-17, logs stabilized for 3m, then node rejoined. but node-19 still shows Xid spikes.

patrick: rolling blacklist: adding node-19 to blacklist list so scheduler won't place new pods there. command: 

```
kubectl label node gpu-node-19 infra/blacklist=true
```

eve: doing customer impact check — 27 orgs reported elevated latencies, 4 orgs started seeing 503s on request paths that hit g1. notified CS with initial message.

naomi: activating fallback: switch conv-4B traffic to conv-2.7B reduced tokens served by heavy models and cut queue rate by ~25% in simulations. want to route at edge.

mike: implemented edge rule to divert conv-4B non-enterprise requests to conv-2.7B with model_fallback header. monitoring.

raj: autoscaler controller logs show API 429 bursts. increasing controller backoff helps but won't create nodes until quota increases.

sarah: added an interim autoscaler policy: allow creation of lower-spec GPUs (p4->p3 equivalents) via fallback amber profile, which uses fewer vram but more pods. wiring done.

jen: we've been seeing driver hotpatch deployments earlier today. possible correlation with kernel driver update rolled last night on a subset of pools. checking gitops.

mike: good catch. ops: which pools received the driver bundle? can we roll that back for suspect nodes?

infra-oncall: driver rollout window was 3132430000 - 3132440000, targeted g1 pools. we've paused rollout. creating rollback patch now.

patrick: rollback in progress to previous driver version for g1. I'll watch for Xid recurrence after rollback.

naomi: CS updated customers with the current mitigation steps and ETA for capacity restoration ~ 45-60m if quota bump comes through; they asked for status updates every 15m.

eve: opening bridge and adding oncall rotation for next 2 hours. handoff to next oncall at 3132468000.

mike: quick command sequences used during triage:

```
kubectl get pods -n ml-serving -o wide | grep Pending
kubectl drain gpu-node-17 --ignore-daemonsets --delete-local-data
gcloud compute instances create --accelerator type=nvidia-tesla-t4,count=1 ...
journalctl -u nvidia-driver -f
```

raj: status update at 3132468050: queue_length down from 1200 -> 720 after model fallback + reroute. node flaps decreased but not eliminated. autoscaler still blocked by quota.

jen: node-19 still showing Xid 43 after rollback attempt; isolating node for forensic logs (t0 snapshot taken).

mike: action items: (1) continue draining + restart drivers on suspect nodes (jen/sarah), (2) maintain routing fallback (mike/naomi), (3) chase quota with cloud ops (mike), (4) CS updates every 15m (eve), (5) prepare capacity cold-start plan if quota denied (raj).

naomi: I'll coordinate cold-start plan: spin up on-prem reserved cluster (dedicated) if cloud fails; that will take ~2-3h to warm.

eve: next status at 3132468180. oncall handoff @3132468200 to sara2. adding notes to incident tracker.

mike: thumbs on bridge. will update after next wave of node restarts. thanks all. :heart:
